In this R-markdown document, this data frame will show at least the univariate logistic modeling, and potentially the multiple logistic modeling, as shown in Xiong et al 2020.

#Step 1: Import Packages, Set Pathways for Data, and Import the Upregulated and Downregulated Genes

```{r}
library(performance)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyr)
library(MASS)
library(stringr)
library(here)
library(broom)
library(DescTools)
library(gtsummary)
library(plotROC)
library(ResourceSelection)

Figure_Export <- file.path(here(),"Figures")
Data_Import <- file.path(here(), "Data")

#Import Data

Upregulated_Genes <- read.delim(file = file.path(Data_Import,"Upregulated_Genes.txt"), header = FALSE)

Downregulated_Genes <- read.delim(file = file.path(Data_Import,"Downregulated_Genes.txt"), header = FALSE)

#Vector of all the Genes
All_Genes <- c(Upregulated_Genes, Downregulated_Genes)

#Convert into one vector
All_Genes <- unlist(All_Genes)


```

#Step 2: Import the Matrix

Import the TCGA-LUAD processed matrix along with ColData which includes the survival and other metadata for this analysis. Additionally, the text files that contains the Upregulated and Downregulated genes in the TCGA-LUAD TCGA dataset and 3 NCBI GEO GSE datasets were imported.

In the methods section of Xiong et al 2020, they noted that for this section of the analysis with modeling, they excluded patients that did not have enough data with respect to TNM(Tumor Growth Risk, Node Invasion, Metastasis Risk). Just like they only used 58 paired patient samples for the Differential Gene Expression Analysis for the TCGA-LUAD data set, they only used a specific segment of the patient data for the uni-logistic and multi-logistic modeling had a total of 370 patients after exclusion of patients that did not have complete TNM Scoring

Unfortunately, they do not explain exactly how that criteria was applied, soassumptions was made to try to get the same # of patients. However, the exact # of patients was not able to be identified and this analysis included 322 patients that had the full data on risk of Tumor Growth Risk Level, Lymph Node Invasion, and Metastasis Risk. This is likely to be one of multiple reasons why the results are not exactly the same.

```{r}
#Import the TCGA-LUAD Matrix Data
TCGA_LUAD_Matrix <- readRDS(file = file.path(Data_Import, "LUAD_counts.rds"))


#Import Metadata, but called Coldata, for the LUAD Dataset
LUAD_Coldata <- readRDS(file = file.path(Data_Import, "LUAD_Coldata.rds"))

#Extract Risk for each of the 3  variables this analysis [Which is analyzing whether a patient will have Low/High Tumor Risk, Low/High Risk of Metastasis, and Low/High Risk of Lymph Invasion]

LUAD_Coldata <- LUAD_Coldata %>% 
  dplyr::select(barcode,  ajcc_pathologic_t, ajcc_pathologic_m, ajcc_pathologic_n) %>%
  mutate(ajcc_pathologic_t = str_extract(ajcc_pathologic_t, "(.{2})"), #Xiong et al 2020 does not say with the differentiation of letter grades, only the numbers, so we combine them (Ex: T1a and T1b will become T1)
         ajcc_pathologic_n = str_extract(ajcc_pathologic_n, "(.{2})")) %>% #This extracts the first 2 characters in the string
  mutate(Risk_Level = case_when(
    ajcc_pathologic_t %in% c("T1","T2") ~ "Low Risk", 
    ajcc_pathologic_t %in% c("T3", "T4") ~ "High Risk", 
    ajcc_pathologic_t %in% c(NA, "TX") ~ "Unknown")) %>%
  mutate(Metastasis = case_when(
    ajcc_pathologic_m %in% c("M0") ~ "No Metastasis",
    ajcc_pathologic_m %in% c("MX", NA) ~ "Unknown Metastasis",
    ajcc_pathologic_m %in% c("M1") ~ "Metastasis")) %>%
  mutate(Lymph_Invasion = case_when(
    ajcc_pathologic_n %in% c("N0") ~ "No Invasion",
    ajcc_pathologic_n %in% c("NX", NA) ~ "Unknown Invasion",
    ajcc_pathologic_n %in% c("N1","N2","N3") ~ "Invasion"))

#Import the Genes that are Upregulated or Downregulated in all 3 datasets
Downregulated_Genes <- read.delim(file = file.path(Data_Import, "Downregulated_Genes.txt"), header = FALSE)
Downregulated_Genes <- Downregulated_Genes[,1]

Upregulated_Genes <- read.delim(file = file.path(Data_Import, "Upregulated_Genes.txt"), header = FALSE)
Upregulated_Genes <- Upregulated_Genes[,1]

#Drop Patient Samples where there is not enough information to perform TNM(Tumor Risk, Node Invasion, Metastasis Risk).
LUAD_Coldata <- LUAD_Coldata %>%
  filter(Risk_Level != "Unknown") %>%
  filter(Metastasis != "Unknown Metastasis") %>% #This will exclude patients that had "MX" as their metastasis status as the X indicates the data was collected, but no determination was made (as far as could be told)
  filter(Lymph_Invasion != "Unknown Invasion") #This will exclude patients that had "NX" as their metastasis status as the X indicates the data was collected, but no determination was made (as far as could be told)

#It appears that exclusion of all the samples that have unknown risk levels does change the results by a decent amount. This is why there is a difference in the univariate modeling between when all samples are included or when samples with only complete TNM scoring is used. However, Xiong et al 2020 excluded those patients, so this code will do the same in spite of no code being able to understand how exactly they were excluded.
```

#Step 3: Normalize the RNA-SEQ Matrix Data by Z-Score

The LUAD Matrix counts were converted into Z-score counts along with filtering of low-count Genes and removal of patients without complete TNM scoring.

```{r}
#Drop when the rowSums of the Gene across all the samples is very low to speed up processing speed for genes of low significance.
keep <- as.vector(rowSums(TCGA_LUAD_Matrix) > 10)

TCGA_LUAD_Matrix <- TCGA_LUAD_Matrix[keep, ]

#Filter for the patients where we have all the Tumor Growth Risk, Lymph Node Invasion, and Metastasis data
TCGA_LUAD_Matrix <- TCGA_LUAD_Matrix[, colnames(TCGA_LUAD_Matrix) %in% LUAD_Coldata$barcode]

# Function to calculate Z-scores with additional options

counts_to_zscore <- function(counts, log_transform = TRUE, pseudo_count = 1) {
# Step 1: Optional log transformation
 if (log_transform) {
# Add pseudo-count to avoid log(0)
 expression_matrix <- log2(counts + pseudo_count)
 } else {
 expression_matrix <- counts
 }

  # Step 2: Calculate Z-scores
  # scale() centers and scales the data by default
  z_scores <- scale(expression_matrix)
  
# Convert to data frame and maintain row names
z_scores_df <- as.data.frame(z_scores)
rownames(z_scores_df) <- rownames(counts)

return(z_scores_df)

}

#Run the Z-scoring
Z_score_TCGA_LUAD <- counts_to_zscore(counts = TCGA_LUAD_Matrix, log_transform = TRUE, pseudo_count = 1)


#VST_stabilized_Counts_LUAD <- readRDS(file = file.path(Data_Import, "VST_transformed_Values.rds"))


#Save Zscore when running
saveRDS(Z_score_TCGA_LUAD, file = file.path(Data_Import, "Z_score_TCGA_LUAD.rds"))
```


#Step 4: Orient the Matrix and ColData

After the Z score was calculated, the data was transposed and oriented to combine the Coldata with relevant metadata and the Z score count matrix.

```{r}
#Step 4.1: Create the Pivoted Matrix needed for the Model to attach the ColData
Combined_Model_Frame <- Z_score_TCGA_LUAD %>%
  t() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(., var = "barcode") 

#If I am trying to use VST stabilized counts rather than Z score
Combined_Model_Frame <- VST_stabilized_Counts_LUAD %>%
  t() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(., var = "barcode") 

Combined_Model_Frame <- Combined_Model_Frame %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c("barcode"), names_to = "Symbols", values_to = "Z_counts") 

#Step 4.2: Add the Coldata (which is one of the metadata types)
Combined_Model_Frame <- Combined_Model_Frame %>%
  left_join(., LUAD_Coldata, by = "barcode")

# Step 4.3: Identify high or low expression for each gene. If a gene's Z-score (which is already normalized) is greater than 0, it means its greater than the average so it counts as a High Expression. If its less than 0, its lower expression
Combined_Model_Frame <- Combined_Model_Frame %>%
  group_by(Symbols) %>%
  mutate(Expression_Level = if_else(Z_counts > 0, "High", "Low")) %>%
  ungroup()
```

#Step 6: Pivot Data Wider to prepare for Logistic Modeling

The dataframe with all the relevant data was  pivoted wider and the outcome variables, whether they were Risk Level of Tumor Growth, or other variables, were converted into a binary to allow the logistic model to work.

```{r}
#Pivot Data Wider to prepare for Logistic Modeling

Univar_model_Frame <- Combined_Model_Frame %>%
  mutate(Expression_Level = if_else(Expression_Level == "High", 1,0)) %>%
  mutate(Risk_Level = if_else(Risk_Level == "High Risk", 1, 0)) %>% #Converting High or Low Risk into a Binary either either a 1 or 0 respectively
  mutate(Lymph_Invasion = case_when(        
    Lymph_Invasion == "No Invasion" ~ 0,
    Lymph_Invasion == "Invasion" ~ 1, 
    TRUE ~ NA)) %>% #Converting  Lymph Note Invasion into a Binary 
  mutate(Metastasis = case_when(
    Metastasis == "No Metastasis" ~ 0,
    Metastasis == "Metastasis" ~ 1, 
    TRUE ~ NA)) %>% #Converting No Metastasis or Metastasis into a Binary
  dplyr::select(-c(ajcc_pathologic_m, ajcc_pathologic_t, ajcc_pathologic_n)) 
```


#Run the univariate logistic model for each gene for the affect on risk level for tumor growth for the Patient

After the Z-scoring was calculated in the previous steps and further data manipulation and cleaning was performed, a univariate model can be run for each gene that was differentially expressed (whether upregulated or downregulated). For each gene that was differentially expressed in all 4 datasets, each of the genes were tested in a univariate model to see if they have a statistically significant effect on the risk of tumor growth. 

This was done by creating a function to perform this analysis for the parameter of interest. Note, although this function does correct for multiple comparisons, as there are many genes being tested, that was not used for the functions for downstream analysis since Xiong et al 2020 did not say whether they corrected for multiple comparisons.

```{r}
#Function to test each gene of interest in a univariate single predictor model
Rapid_Univariate_Analysis <- function(data = dataframe, outcome_variable = "Risk_Level", Genes_of_Interest = NULL, Symbol_Column = "Symbols"){
 
#Create Dataframe to store model information
output_frame <- matrix(nrow = length(Genes_of_Interest), ncol = 4)
colnames(output_frame) <- c("Gene_Name","p.value", "method", "coeff")
output_frame <- as.data.frame(output_frame)

#Choose the Column with all the Symbols
  SYMBOLS <- data[[Symbol_Column]]

#Filter out non-import genes prior to analysis
input_frame <- data %>%
  filter(SYMBOLS %in% Genes_of_Interest)

#Run Loop to identify for each gene if it is statistically significant along in a univariate model
for (i in 1:length(Genes_of_Interest)){
  
  #Choose Gene
  Gene <- All_Genes[i]
  
  #Create Dataframe with column of Interest
  DATA <- input_frame %>%
    filter(Symbols == Gene) %>%
    dplyr::select(c("Symbols","Z_counts", outcome_variable))
  
  #Create Model
  model <- glm(formula = DATA[[outcome_variable]] ~ Z_counts, 
                    data = DATA,
                    family = "binomial"(link=logit))
  
  model_tidy <- tidy(model)
  
  ##Extract Information of Interest
  
  #Gene Name
  output_frame[i,1] <- Gene
  #P.value
  output_frame[i,2] <- model_tidy[2, "p.value"] 

  #Method
  output_frame[i,3] <- model$method
  #Coefficient
  output_frame[i,4] <- model$coefficients[2]
  
  #Keep Track which gene is being analyzed
  print(paste("Gene", i, "out of", length(Genes_of_Interest)))
  
}

 #Corrected P value (Done by Bonferroni Hochberg by default)
  
  output_frame[["p.adjusted"]] <- p.adjust(output_frame[["p.value"]], method = "BH")
  
return(output_frame)
}
```

Run the Rapid Univariate Model for Risk of Tumor Growth

```{r}
#Run Univariate Model Analysis on each genes effect on Risk Level for Tumor Growth
Risk_Level_Dataframe_2 <- Rapid_Univariate_Analysis(data = Univar_model_Frame,
                          Genes_of_Interest = All_Genes,
                          outcome_variable = "Risk_Level")

#Graph the results 
Risk_Level_Dataframe_2 %>%
  mutate(coeff_variable = if_else(coeff > 0, "Pos","Neg")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=coeff, y = -log10(p.value),
             color = coeff_variable))+
  geom_point(aes(size = abs(coeff)))+
  theme_bw()+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Neg" = "skyblue","Pos" = "orange"))+
  geom_text(hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.05,
            label = paste(Risk_Level_Dataframe_2$Gene_Name), color = "black")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "black")+
   labs(title = "Univariate model of each gene for effect on risk level of \n new Tumor Growth")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

#Save equivalent graph to Figure 3a (Note, I am not sure why the graphs have changed some, so I am going to save both graphs but changing the name of this one slightly)

ggsave(filename = file.path(Figure_Export, "Univariate_Model_TumorRiskModel_Fig3a.png"))

#Filter out non-significant genes
tumorgrowthrisk <- Risk_Level_Dataframe_2 %>%
  filter(p.value < 0.05)

tumorgrowthrisk <- tumorgrowthrisk$Gene_Name

#Save Genes
write.table(tumorgrowthrisk, file = file.path(Data_Import, "TumorGrowthRisk_Genes_Univariate_Model.txt"))

```

#Proceed to Multi-logistic Analysis

After Xiong et al 2020 performed univariate analysis on all the differentially expressed genes, they isolated all the genes that were found to have a statistically significant impact on either Tumor Growth Risk, Lymph Invasion Risk, or Metastasis risk. The first code chunk will be for the genes on elevated Tumor Risk with all of those genes. They showed that there is quite a bit of collinearity between the genes.

```{r}
#All the genes that are significant are combined if I want to use that in any scenario in any of the 3 univariate models previously
#sig_genes <- c(tumorgrowthrisk, metastasis_genes, lymphgenes)

#saveRDS(sig_genes, file = file.path(Data_Import, "Significant_Genes_From_Univariate_Model.rds"))

#Create dataframe for multivariate Model
multivariate_model_frame <- Univar_model_Frame %>% 
  filter(Symbols %in% tumorgrowthrisk) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Lymph_Invasion, Expression_Level, Metastasis)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "Symbols", values_from = "Z_counts")

```


The multi-logistic model will be now be run manually with all the genes that are impactful on the risk level of Tumor growth. This is kept for transparency sake, but again it is just an example to show how the manually the multiple logistic regression is/was performed.

```{r}
#Create Formula including all of these models
formula <- reformulate(tumorgrowthrisk, response = "Risk_Level")

multi_logistic_tumorgrowth_model <- glm(formula, 
                                     data = multivariate_model_frame,
                                     family = "binomial"(link=logit))
#Check Summary 
summary(multi_logistic_tumorgrowth_model)

#Check Model Assumptions
check_model(multi_logistic_tumorgrowth_model)

#Unsurprisingly, there is some collinearity for multiple genes. Therefore, a test for correlation between the genes will need to be done
Univar_model_Frame %>%
  filter(Symbols %in% tumorgrowthrisk) %>%
  select(c(barcode, Symbols, Z_counts)) %>% # Filtering for all of the Genes that are alone significant impact on Tumor Growth Risk
  pivot_wider(., names_from = "Symbols", values_from = "Z_counts") %>% dplyr::select(-barcode) %>%
  cor(.) %>%
  corrplot::corrplot()

#Look at Log-Odds and OR for a 1 point increase in the Z score
multi_logistic_tumorgrowth_model %>%
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE)

multi_logistic_tumorgrowth_model %>%
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = FALSE)

multi_logistic_tumorgrowth_model %>%
  tidy()

#Identify C-stat (Area under the ROC Curve) and AUC
Cstat(multi_logistic_tumorgrowth_model)

#AIC value
multi_logistic_tumorgrowth_model$aic


```

#Perform Manual Backwards step regression

Although Xiong et al 2020 does not explain what type of stepwise regression. After the model with all of the genes effects on tumor growth risk level, the gene with the highest p-value, or least significant, was removed and the model was moved again by backwards selection. There is awareness that this isn't typically the best type of model designing framework, but for the sake of trying to reproduce their model, it was done.

```{r}
#Genes to be removed
Genes_removed <- c()
Genes_removed <- c()
#Genes_Left
gene_select <- tumorgrowthrisk[!tumorgrowthrisk %in% Genes_removed]

#Create Formula including all of these models
formula <- reformulate(gene_select, response = "Risk_Level")

#Run and Check Model
multi_tumorgrowth_model_0 <- glm(formula, 
                                     data = multivariate_model_frame,
                                     family = "binomial"(link=logit))

summary(multi_tumorgrowth_model_0)

#Identify C-stat (Area under the ROC Curve)
Cstat(multi_tumorgrowth_model_0)

#AIC value
multi_tumorgrowth_model_0$aic
```

#Backwards selection by written function

Alternatively, instead of manually performing the backwards selection, a function was written to manually perform backwards selection for each of the genes in the multiple logistic model. There is awareness that backwards selection is typically not a good method for choosing model parameters, but that is what Xiong et al 2020 appeared to do. 

This function will run backwards selection until all the predictors are statistically significant, and then select the model with the lowest AIC value (which is indicative of the best model among all options) and then return that model in the output. This is still the case even if a couple parameters which are not statistically significant are added back in

Backward_Selection_Test[[1]] is the dataframe where the changes in Cstat/ROC and AIC of the model after removal of the gene
Backward_Selection_Test[[2]] is the model where all the predictors are statistically significant
Backward_Selection_Test[[3]] is the optimized model based on AIC values

Furthermore, an explanation of each column will be done:

Iteration = The iteration of the model, where iteration 1 means that no genes has been removed.

Gene_Name_Removed <- The Gene that was removed from the model in this iteration.

Cstat/ROC <- The Cstat/ROC of the model after the gene is removed from the model.

pvalue_prior_to_removal <- **IMPORTANT NOTE**: This is the p-value of the gene in the model prior to being removed. So, for each row, the gene that was removed will have the Gene removed, the p value of the gene before it was removed, and then the Cstat/ROC and AIC of the model **after** removal of the gene.

AIC-value <- The value of the AIC after removal of the gene.

```{r}
Backward_Selection_Test <- function(Gene_List = Gene_List, input_frame = model_frame, outcome_variable = "Risk_Level"){

### Run Initial Model
  
  #Set Iteration
  i <- 1
  
  #Set blank vector of vector of removed genes
  List_of_removed_Genes <- c()
  
  #Create Dataframe
  dataframe <- matrix(ncol = 5, nrow = length(Gene_List))
  dataframe <- as.data.frame(dataframe)
  colnames(dataframe) <- c("Iteration","Gene_Name_Removed", "C-stat/ROC", "pvalue_prior_to_removal", "AIC-value")
  
  #Run Initial Model
  model_formula <- reformulate(Gene_List, response = outcome_variable)
  
  model <- glm(formula = model_formula, 
               data = input_frame,
               family = "binomial"(link=logit))
 #Iteration 
dataframe[i,1] <- 1

#Initially No Genes Removed
dataframe[i,2] <- NA
   
#Identify C-stat (Area under the ROC Curve) for initial model
dataframe[i, 3] <- Cstat(model)

#Look at Model
model_tidy <- model %>% 
  tidy() %>%
  mutate(p_adjusted = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) %>%
  arrange(., by = desc(p.value))

#Access p-value of the Gene that was removed (For the first iteration, it should be NA since no genes were removed)
dataframe[i,4] <- NA

#AIC value for initial model
dataframe[i, 5] <- model$aic

print("Finished Iteration 1")

#Test_factor

test_factor <- any(model_tidy[["p.value"]] > 0.05) 


## Run Loop as the backwards selection occurs

while(test_factor == TRUE){
  
  #Isolate Gene to be removed from model
  Gene_to_be_Removed <- model_tidy[1,1]
  
  List_of_removed_Genes <- c(List_of_removed_Genes, Gene_to_be_Removed)
  
  
  #Select the Iteration
  i <- i + 1
  
  #Access p-value of the Gene in the model before its removed and a new model is ran
  dataframe[i,4] <- model_tidy[1,5]
  
  #Remove the de-selected Genes
  Genes_Selected <- Gene_List[!Gene_List %in% List_of_removed_Genes]
  
  #Run New Model
  model_formula <- reformulate(Genes_Selected, response = outcome_variable)
  
  
  model <- glm(model_formula, 
               data = input_frame,
               family = "binomial"(link=logit))
  #Iteration
dataframe[i,1] <- i

#Gene that was Removed
dataframe[i,2] <- Gene_to_be_Removed

#Identify C-stat (Area under the ROC Curve) for initial model
dataframe[i, 3] <- Cstat(model)

#AIC value for initial model
dataframe[i, 5] <- model$aic

#Look at Model
model_tidy <- model %>%
  tidy() %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(p_adjusted = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) %>%
  arrange(., by = desc(p.value))

#Extract p.value (Temporarily ommited for now since I want the p-value of in the model before the gene is removed, not after)
#dataframe[i,4] <- model_tidy[1,5]

#Checking Progress
print(paste("Finished Iteration", i))

#Test Factor Check
test_factor <- any(model_tidy[["p.value"]] > 0.05) 

}

#Remove rows that are unneeded until all the remaining predictors are statistically significant
dataframe <- dataframe[1:i, ]

dataframe_with_model <- list(dataframe, model)

## Choose the Optimized Model with the lowest AIC value

#identify index of the gene removed with the lowest AIC model
index <- dataframe %>% 
  mutate(`AIC-value` = as.numeric(`AIC-value`)) %>%
  slice_min(`AIC-value`)

#
index <- as.integer(index[1])
#
order_of_aic <- dataframe %>% 
filter(Iteration <= index) %>%
drop_na(Gene_Name_Removed)

#

genes_final_model <- as.vector(order_of_aic[["Gene_Name_Removed"]])
                               
##Run the optimized Model with the lowest AIC value

#Remove the de-selected Genes
  Genes_Selected_optimized <- Gene_List[!Gene_List %in% genes_final_model]
  
#Run Optimized Model
  model_formula_optimized <- reformulate(Genes_Selected_optimized, response = outcome_variable)
  
  model_optimized <- glm(model_formula_optimized, 
               data = input_frame,
               family = "binomial"(link=logit))
  

##Attach the optimized model along with the dataframe that filtered out each gene individually
export <- list(dataframe, model, model_optimized)

return(export)

}

```

The use of backwards selection function, consistent with stepwise selection used by Xiong et al 2020, was used to identify and narrow down which genes are going to be statistically significant in a multi-logistic model on the effect of Tumor Growth Risk.

```{r}
#Step 1: Run the Backwards Selection Function to do the backward selection work that I perform above
Tumor_Risk_Model <- Backward_Selection_Test(input_frame = multivariate_model_frame,
                        Gene_List = tumorgrowthrisk,
                        outcome_variable = "Risk_Level")

###Step 1.5: Using the stepAIC function from the MASS package instead of using my custom function to see if they come up with the same result.
tumor_formula <- reformulate(tumorgrowthrisk, response = "Risk_Level")

Tumor_Risk_Model_stepAIC <- glm(formula = tumor_formula,
                        family = "binomial"(link=logit),
                        data = multivariate_model_frame)

Tumor_Risk_Model_stepAIC <- stepAIC(Tumor_Risk_Model_stepAIC , direction = "backward")
####

##Step 2: Look at the results from my backwards_selection_function and the stepAIC function

#Look at the Dataframe of the iterations of the model
Tumor_Risk_Model[[1]]

#Look at the Model with all statistically significant predictors even if it doesn't have the lowest AIC
summary(Tumor_Risk_Model[[2]])

#Look at AIC Optimized Model
summary(Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]])

summary(Tumor_Risk_Model_stepAIC)

#Both my function and the stepAIC function from the MASS package come to the same result which is good news.





###Step 3: Use AIC optimized Model and Check Model Assumptions

#Check Model Assumptions ---> The Binned residuals continously has certain ones outside of the curve, but overall most of the points are within the error bounds
check_model(Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]]) 
# Passes all the assumptions except the homogeneity of variance, but because its a logistic model, that is not a good way to measure model assumptions.

#Check the Linearity of the logit for the Logistic Model!
probabilities <- predict(Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]], type = "response")


#Calculate the Logit --> Log Odds linearity
logit <- log(probabilities / (1 - probabilities))
num <- multivariate_model_frame %>% dplyr::select(-barcode)

Linearity_of_Logit_Dataframe <- data.frame(
  logit     = rep(logit, ncol(num)),
  predictor = rep(names(num), each = nrow(num)),
  value     = unlist(num)
)

#Look at Logit Graph
Linearity_of_Logit_Dataframe %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=logit, y = value))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "loess")+
  facet_wrap(~predictor)

#Based on this test, we can confirm that it passes the linearity of logit test because each of the predictors is linearly related to the log odds of the outcome. ---> Pass






#Step 4: Homser-Lemeshow test on model fit

HL <- hoslem.test(x = Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]]$y, y = fitted(Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]]), g = 10) 

#Step 5: Calculate the AUC (area under the curve) of the Cstat/ROC curve and graph

AUC <- round(Cstat(Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]]), 2)

#Using the ROCR/plotROC packages, I can create a ROC plot from the ROC

#Create the "Prediction Data" which I will just pull from the original dataframe
mtgm <- multivariate_model_frame %>% dplyr::select(barcode, all_of(tumorgrowthrisk))

#Predicted Results
mtgm$Predicted_Risk_Level <- predict(object = Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]],
                                 newdata = mtgm, 
                                 type = c("response"))
#Real_Results
mtgm$Risk_Level <- multivariate_model_frame$Risk_Level

#Graph the ROC Graph of the Optimized Model
ggplot(mtgm, aes(d = Risk_Level,                      # true disease label
                     m = Predicted_Risk_Level)) +     # continuous biomarker that is predicted
    geom_roc(labels = FALSE) +                         # draw ROC curve
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0)+
    annotate("text", x = .9, y = .250,                 # add AUC score
             label = paste("AUC =", AUC))+
   annotate("text", x = 0.9, y = .45,                      # add Hoslem.test results
             label = paste("Hoslem-Lemeshow test \n p =", round(HL$p.value, 2)))+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(x = "Sensitivity", y = "Specificity",
       title = "ROC Curve of the Final Model for the Impact of Differentially Expressed \n Genes on Tumor Growth Risk")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

#Save plot
ggsave(filename = file.path(Figure_Export,"Multiple_Logistic_TumorGrowth_RiskLevel_ROC_Fig_3e.png"))


```

#Create Graph of Coefficients for each gene

```{r}
#Calculate the 95$ confident Interval
risklevelCI <- as.data.frame(confint(Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]]))

coefficients <- as.data.frame(Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]]$coefficients)
coefficients <- Tumor_Risk_Model[[3]]$coefficients
#Add Coeff
risklevelCI$coeff <- coefficients

#Graph Results
risklevelCI <- risklevelCI %>%
  rownames_to_column(., var = "Genes")

risklevelCI %>% 
  filter(Genes != "(Intercept)") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= Genes, y = coeff))+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = `2.5 %`, ymax = `97.5 %`),
                width = 0.075, linewidth = 2, color = "skyblue")+
  geom_point(color = "tomato4", size = 2)+
  theme_classic() +
  coord_flip() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)+
  labs(y = "coeff(95%CI)")+
  theme(axis.title.y.left = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y.left = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.title.x.bottom = element_text(face = "bold"))

ggsave(filename = file.path(Figure_Export, "Optimized_Multiple_Logistic_Model_TumorGrowthRisk_3D.png"))
```

#Perform Backward Selection on the Genes that impact Lymph Node Invasion

```{r}
#Create dataframe for multivariate Model
lymph_frame <- Univar_model_Frame %>% 
  filter(Symbols %in% lymphgenes) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Risk_Level, Expression_Level, Metastasis)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "Symbols", values_from = "Z_counts")

#####Use Backwards Selection Function to optimize model 

Backwards_Lymph_Invasion <- Backward_Selection_Test(input_frame = lymph_frame, 
                               Gene_List = lymphgenes,
                               outcome_variable = "Lymph_Invasion")

#Look at the Dataframe of the iterations of the model
Backwards_Lymph_Invasion[[1]]

#Look at Model with only significant predictors
summary(Backwards_Lymph_Invasion[[2]])

#Look at the Optimized Model
summary(Backwards_Lymph_Invasion[[3]])


##Use the model that is optimized for AIC

#Check Model Assumptions ---> The Binned residuals have at a few points outside the scale
check_model(Backwards_Lymph_Invasion[[3]])

#####Run the Hosmer-Lemeshow Goodness of Fit Test where a p value < 0.05 means that we reject the null that the model fits the data well. Therefore, since the p value is greater than 0.05, we can accept that the model accurately fits the model.

HL <- hoslem.test(x = Backwards_Lymph_Invasion[[3]]$y, y = fitted(Backwards_Lymph_Invasion[[3]]), g = 10) 

####Look at ROC Curve

#Look at the AUC under the ROC Curve which is rounded

AUC <- round(Cstat(Backwards_Lymph_Invasion[[3]]), 2)

#Create the "Prediction Data" which I will just pull from the original dataframe
mtgm <- lymph_frame %>% dplyr::select(barcode, all_of(lymphgenes))

#Predicted Results
mtgm$Predicted_Lymph_Invasion <- predict(object = Backwards_Lymph_Invasion[[3]],
                                 newdata = mtgm, 
                                 type = c("response"))
#Real_Results
mtgm$Risk_Level <-lymph_frame$Lymph_Invasion

#Graph the ROC Graph
ggplot(mtgm, aes(d = Risk_Level,                          # true disease label
                     m = Predicted_Lymph_Invasion)) +     # continuous biomarker that is predicted
    geom_roc(labels = F) +               # draw ROC curve
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0)+
    annotate("text", x = 0.9, y = .25,                    # add AUC score
             label = paste("AUC =", AUC))+
  annotate("text", x = 0.9, y = .45,                      # add Hoslem.test results
             label = paste("Hoslem-Lemeshow test \n p =", round(HL$p.value, 2)))+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(x = "Sensitivity", y = "Specificity",
       title = "ROC Curve of the Final Model for the Impact of Differentially Expressed \n Genes on Lymph Invasion")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

ggsave(filename = file.path(Figure_Export, "Multiple_Logistic_Lymph_Invasion_ROC_Fig_3g.png"))
```
